parsed_response.reasoning: The diff genuinely changes the public Calendar interface: packages/types/Calendar.d.ts changes `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent)` to `createEvent(event: CalendarEvent, credentialId: number)` — a required second parameter on an exported interface. Note that within the repo this does NOT actually break the shown implementations (LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService, and BaseCalendarService still declare `createEvent(event)` and TypeScript structurally permits implementations with fewer parameters), so the 'breaks other implementations in the PR' portion is overstated. However, the substantive concern stands: this is a non-backwards-compatible change to a public/app-store-facing contract (Cal.com app-store packages implement this interface) made without a deprecation path or default value for credentialId, e.g. `credentialId?: number`. A maintainer would want to know this when deciding whether to ship or soften the signature, since external/third-party calendar app implementations calling the old one-arg form and consumers implementing this interface are silently forced to migrate.

judged_text: Breaking change to public Calendar interface signature: createEvent(event, credentialId) now requires a second number argument without deprecation, breaking CalendarService.ts abstract base and other implementations not updated in the PR
